title: Probe-driven Fidelity Lattice and Quant Hedging Playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a practical, probe-driven approach for managing a fidelity lattice (a graded set of model quantization / execution modes) and an automated hedging policy that routes traffic, triggers fallbacks, and controls rollouts. It is intended for model-onboarding engineers, SREs supporting inference fleets, and evaluation teams responsible for quality regressions during quant migration.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token cost by opportunistically using lower-fidelity execution while maintaining user-facing quality SLOs.
- Detect and contain fidelity-induced regressions early using probes and live-slice telemetry.
- Provide deterministic rollback and hedging rules that integrate with Canary/A/B and Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to sequence generation models (chat, completions, rerankers) served by the Redwood runtime.
- Assumes model artifacts have at least two quantization variants (baseline_fp16/fp32, quant8/aq8, and a low-memory int4-like option).
- Requires probe infrastructure (eval harness shadow runs, slice tagging, and real-time quality sensors) already configured per service.

Key concepts:
1) Fidelity lattice: an ordered list of model variants by fidelity and cost. Example lattice levels: HIGHEST -> baseline_fp16, MEDIUM -> quant8, LOW -> int4_sparse.
2) Probe cohort: a lightweight, representative probe set for a service slice (user intent cluster) used to surface coherence/regression signals during shadow and live checks.
3) Hedging policy: pre-authorized rules that route live traffic to fallback fidelity levels (or alternate models) when telemetry crosses thresholds.
4) Safety envelope: SLOs, noise budgets, and automated conditions under which a rollout must pause or roll back.

Fidelity lattice (example table):
| level | variant id | expected latency delta | token-cost ratio | expected coherence impact | owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| HIGHEST | m-xl-baseline-fp16 | +0 ms | 1.00x | baseline | model-onboard-team |
| MEDIUM | m-xl-quant8 | -12% | 0.62x | small risk (templated answers) | runtime-ops |
| LOW | m-xl-int4-sparse | -28% | 0.38x | medium risk (hallucination/formatting) | runtime-ops |

Quality and telemetry signals to monitor:
- Probe pass rate (primary): fraction of probe inputs where the fidelity variant matches baseline acceptance criteria (semantic match >= configured threshold).
- Drift score: embedding similarity change vs baseline on anchor prompts.
- Latency tail (p95, p99) and token-level throughput differential.
- Functioncall fidelity: percentage of function calls with parsed arguments matching ground truth.
- Regression surface: rate of new failure slices (per 10k requests) compared to baseline.
- Cost delta: observed per-token spend change vs baseline window.

Release criteria (pre-flight checklist):
- Unit tests and model verification complete (see onboarding-checklist).
- Shadow run against representative probe cohort for 24–72 hours with:
  - Probe pass rate >= 99% for MEDIUM, >= 95% for LOW (adjust per service risk).
  - No new high-severity slice with >1% traffic exposure.
  - Latency tail within configured SLO increase (default p95 <= baseline_p95 + 20ms).
- Sign-off from the model owner and runtime-ops (explicit reviewer approval entry in related_pages).

Automated hedging policy (example rules):
1. Live routing preconditions:
   - Start: 0% -> MEDIUM hedged traffic for canary (sampled 1%)
   - Expand to 5% if 24h shadow probes pass
2. Real-time triggers (immediate action):
   - If Probe pass rate drops by >2.5 percentage points vs rolling baseline -> immediate shift to previous lattice level for affected slices and create incident with severity P2.
   - If new regression slice rate >0.5% for traffic-weighted slices -> pause expansion and throttle to 50% of target.
3. Escalation windows (if degraded but not catastrophic):
   - After 30 minutes of degraded probe pass rate, revert to baseline for the slice, trigger auto-bisect job, and open a triage ticket.

Runbook: responding to a hedging trigger
1. Triage owner assignment: runtime-ops oncall (first 15min), then model-onboard lead if root cause is model/quant.
2. Immediate mitigation:
   - Execute automated rollback: set route override to previous fidelity level for impacted slice (CLI example below).
   - Notify SLO dashboard channel and oncall pager.
3. Collect artifacts (automated):
   - Shadow logs for affected requests (include seed, tokenization, KV hit/miss).
   - Probe-level diffs and embedding drift snapshots.
   - Quantization metadata (quant table version, calibration seed).
4. Investigation steps (ordered):
   - Reproduce locally with failing probes and salted seeds.
   - Run deterministic replay using eval harness (seeded run, same environment).
   - Check kernel and scheduling changes in runtime release notes (matching release tag).
   - If repro is consistent, open model regression PR and block rollout.

Example CLI snippets and rollout config:
- Rollout override (CLI):
  redwood routing set --service payments-ner --slice intent:address-parse --variant m-xl-baseline-fp16 --reason "auto-rollback: probe drop"

- Canary rollout YAML (snippet):
  rollout: |
    name: m-xl-quant8-canary
    start_percent: 1
    target_percent: 20
    expansion_window_hours: 24
    probes: sample-probe-cohort:small
    hedging:
      probe_pass_delta_threshold: 2.5
      slice_regression_threshold_pct: 0.5
      auto_revert: true

Safety envelope and thresholds (defaults):
- Probe pass rate delta: 2.5 percentage points
- New high-severity slice threshold: 0.1% of traffic
- Regression slice threshold (aggregate): 0.5%
- Latency p95 uplift allowed: 20ms absolute
- Cost reduction floor: do not reduce fidelity if expected QoE loss > 3% without explicit Product sign-off

Telemetry dashboards and alerts to configure:
- Probe Health dashboard: time-series for each probe cohort (pass rate, drift, variant compare).
- Fidelity Delta dashboard: comparative panel for cost, latency, and pass rates across lattice levels.
- Auto-hedge activity log: event stream showing automatic route changes, triggers, and revert actions.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - P1: Probe pass rate delta >= 5 points for any high-traffic slice (page + Slack)
  - P2: Probe pass rate delta in [2.5, 5) points for 10 minutes (Slack + ticket)
  - P3: Latency p99 uplift > 50ms for 5 minutes (ticket)

Integration with evaluation pipelines:
- Shadow orchestration: use the eval-harness shadow runner with seeded probe cohorts to continuously score quant variants.
- Periodic full-evals: weekly long-tail sweep across annotated slices before expanding canary percentage.
- Regression bisect: if automated bisect identifies a suspected change (quant table, prompt rewrite, runtime patch), link the bisect result to the rollback ticket.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- model-onboard-team: provide fidelity variants, expected degradation notes, and probe cohorts.
- runtime-ops: implement hedging automation, maintain rollout service, and own immediate rollback actions.
- applied-ml/evals: design and maintain probe cohorts and acceptance thresholds.
- eng-sre: configure SLO-aware alerting and oncall rotations.

Post-incident playbook and postmortem criteria:
- Required when any P1 auto-hedge or manual rollback affects >1% of traffic or causes customer-facing errors.
- Postmortem should include: timeline, probe diffs, replay artifacts, quant metadata, root-cause hypothesis, corrective actions, and required changes to the lattice or thresholds.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigation hints
- Tokenization mismatch after quant calibration: re-run tokenization-consistency test; if failing, reject quant build.
- Functioncall syntax drift: tighten functioncall parsing acceptance check and increase probe weight for functioncall patterns.
- Long-context coherence drop with int4: restrict LOW-level usage to short sequences only via route rules.

Related pages:
- related: [onboarding-fidelity-sla-and-noise-budget-manifest], [quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook], [probe-lifecycle-annotation-economics-playbook]

Contact and escalation list:
- Primary: runtime-ops oncall (pager on Slack channel #runtime-hedging, alias: runtime-ops-oncall)
- Secondary: Priya Raman (author) priya@redwood.ai
- Model owner: listed per-variant in the fidelity lattice table

Change log:
- 2026-11-03: created (Priya Raman).
- 2026-12-15: added automated bisect integration and default thresholds (review: Diego Morales).
- 2027-01-12: tightened probe pass thresholds for MEDIUM level after field testing (review: Aalyssa Chen).

Notes and implementation guidance:
- Treat the fidelity lattice as a living document: update variant ids and owners each release.
- Calibrate thresholds per-service: low-risk rerankers can use more aggressive low-fidelity tiers than user-facing assistants.
- Keep probe cohorts small but representative; compute power for probes should be ~0.1–0.5% of production traffic for continuous shadowing.

End of document.
